23日晚上，我在塔尼娅的圣名日聚会上……一个阴暗、恐怖的地窖公寓，由一个小房间和一个厨房组成。在我读了墙上贴的日历页和旧报纸，更确切地说，是在无聊了一个小时之后，餐桌摆好了。没多少喝的，也没多少吃的，没有音乐。无聊透顶。总而言之，加兰金得出了正确的结论：你还能指望这些人什么呢？

On the evening of the 23rd I was at Tanya’s name-day party . . . A black, dreadful cellar apartment consisting of a small room and a kitchen. After I read pages from the calendar and the old newspapers, which are glued to the wall, or more precisely: after an hour of boredom, the table was laid. There wasn’t much to drink, not much food, and no music. Awful boring. All in all, Galankin made the right conclusion: What can you expect from these people?
22日，波琳娜·拉科尼克打来电话。她邀请我和尼古拉（加兰金）去她公寓参加舞会。舞跳得很精彩，我结识了一个不同的社交圈，比我迄今接触的圈子更有文化，也完全不同……

On the 22nd Polina Lakernik called. She invited me and Nikolai [Galankin] to a dance at her apartment. The dancing was splendid, I got to know a different society, more cultured and totally different from the one with which I have mingled so far . . .
27日，我和波琳娜去红军中央大厦的滑冰场滑冰。
斯捷潘寻求波琳娜、尼古拉等人的陪伴，不仅仅是为了他们的“文化”吸引力。他表达了对友谊的需求，希望有人能分享他的担忧、冲突、疑虑以及他最内心深处的本质。然而，这些愿望与保持警惕的必要性发生了冲突，他必须确保自己的阶级出身秘密不会泄露。
On the 27th I went ice-skating with Polina on the skating-rink of the Central House of the Red Army.

Stepan sought the company of Polina, Nikolai, and others not for the sake of their “cultured” appeal alone. He voiced a need for friendship, for people with whom he could share his worries, conflicts, and doubts, his innermost essence. Yet these desires ran up against the necessity to remain guarded, to be sure the secret of his class origins would not leak out.

朋友和同事写给波德卢布内的信件表明，他那种警觉的行为并没有逃过他们的注意。1933年，他与维罗妮卡·伊万诺娃交往，她难得是一位出身于“苏联贵族”的受过良好教育的“有文化”女孩。他们开始通信，根据当时的理想人格讨论彼此的感情。他告诉她，他的目标是“用大脑的力量压制内心感情的迸发”。通过像机器一样过着严格理性化的生活，他希望化身为“新人”的理想。但维罗妮卡提醒他，新人有一个大脑和一颗心，而不是两个大脑，并敦促他改掉“掩饰感情和情绪”的习惯：“你很孤独，在个人生活中很孤独。那是因为你想得到的很多，却几乎不想给予回报……你是一个隐士，不幸的是，你还是个怀疑论者。为什么？我不知道。”斯捷潘被维罗妮卡的信吓坏了。她似乎看穿了他的秘密。他立即断绝了与她的联系。多年后，他会怀念地想起与维罗妮卡的相遇，并哀叹自己未能维持这段关系。
一位共青团员里沙特·海布林对斯捷潘性格的评价则不那么客气。在两人因波德卢布内拒绝承担的一项共青团任务发生争执后，里沙特给他写了一封信，指出斯捷潘做错了，并暗示这是由于他未能调动意志去克服自己的“消极特质”。信的结尾是：“不要把我的话看作是责备，而应看作是支持提高我们文化水平的论据。里沙特。”
这些信件不仅揭示了波德卢布内周围的人对他的看法；它们还表明，他的同龄人也像他一样，努力将自己塑造成那个时代的进步青年，参与自我完善、相互观察和纠正的实践。

Letters written to Podlubny by friends and colleagues indicate that his watchful behavior did not escape their attention. In 1933 he became involved with Veronika Ivanova, for once a “cultured” and educated girl hailing from the “Soviet aristocracy.” They started a correspondence in which they discussed their feelings for each other in light of the personality ideal of the time. His goal, he told her, was to “suppress the outpouring of inner feelings with the power of the brain.” By living a strictly rationalist life in the image of a machine, he hoped to incarnate the ideal of the “new man.” But Veronika reminded him that the new man had a brain and a heart, not two brains, and urged him to drop his habit of “masking your feelings and emotions”: “You are lonely, lonely in your personal life. And that is because you want to get very much and give almost nothing in return . . . You are a hermit and, unfortunately, a skeptic on top of that. Why? I don’t know.” Stepan was alarmed by Veronika’s letter. She seemed to have divined his secret. He immediately broke off contact with her. Years later he would wistfully recall his encounters with Veronika and mourn his failure to make the relationship last.

A fellow komsomolist, Rishat Khaibulin, was less kind in his assessment of Stepan’s personality. After an altercation between the two about a Komsomol assignment that Podlubny refused to take on, Rishat sent him a letter, pointing out that Stepan had acted wrongly, and suggesting that this resulted from his failure to mobilize his will against his “negative traits.” The letter ended: “Take my statement not as a reproach but as an argument in favor of raising our cultural level. Rishat.”

These letters not only shed light on the way people around Podlubny saw him; they also show that Podlubny’s efforts to define himself as a progressive young man of his age were shared by his peers, who were engaged in similar practices of self-perfection, mutual observation, and correction.

波德卢布内在日记中抱怨他在莫斯科的生活中没有可以倾诉的人，尽管这威胁到他伪装身份的保全，但他仍与乌克兰儿时的朋友保持着积极的通信。他的许多老朋友都离开了乌克兰；有些像他的家人一样在“消灭富农”运动中遭到清算，另一些则自愿前往城市和工业区。在给他们的信中，波德卢布内总把自己描绘成一个勤奋且“有文化”的工人和学生，自豪地提到自己的薪水，并吹嘘莫斯科的生活比“边陲”地区优越得多；他的堂表亲科尔内·克里沃鲁卡就住在边陲。反过来，在远东服役的科尔内强调了红军官兵在当地居民中开展的文明化工作。也许比波德卢布内的日记本身更有力的是，这两个富农之子之间的通信——他们向彼此展示为模范苏联公民——展示了自我改造的革命命令是如何被内化为私人身份的，甚至对于那些被政权视为潜在反革命分子的目标人群也是如此。

波德卢布内在1934年和1936年两次回乌克兰家乡过节。他在那里发现的现实证明与他新建立的“有文化”青年的抱负格格不入。他对村民缺乏教育、普遍的父权文化以及集体农庄生活的悲惨感到震惊。相比之下，他刻意以一个受过教育、穿着体面的莫斯科人的形象出现，以赢得村里的尊重。在1936年访问期间，当时他已经是一名学生，他戴着假眼镜来给村民留下深刻印象。他们的反应各不相同：年轻女孩崇拜他，但也有人抱怨在消灭富农时对富农的处理不够彻底。最终，波德卢布内不得不缩短行程逃走。朋友们告诉他，地方当局想逮捕他。
波德卢布内的姿态揭示出他是苏联体制的受益者，这个体制赋予了他权威、文化，并让他确信自己已从农村生活的愚昧中解放出来。特别是他与乌克兰旧家亲友的联系让他深切感受到，他在莫斯科（这个国家的文化中心）的生活之外，没有任何可行的替代方案——尽管那里的生活是有条件的且不稳定的。

Complaining in his diary that in his Moscow life he had no one to confide in, Podlubny maintained an active correspondence with childhood friends from Ukraine, despite the threat to the preservation of his false identity. Many of his old friends had left Ukraine; some had been dekulakized like his family, others had left on their own for the cities and industrial sites. In his letters to them, Podlubny invariably portrayed himself as an industrious and “cultured” worker and student, proudly mentioning his salary and boasting about life in Moscow compared with the living standards on the “periphery,” where one correspondent, his cousin Kornei Krivoruka, lived. In turn, Kornei, who served in the Red Army and was stationed in the far east, underscored the civilizing work that the Red Army men conducted among the local population. Perhaps even more forcefully than Podlubny’s diary itself, this correspondence between two sons of kulaks, who presented themselves to each other as model Soviet citizens, demonstrates the way the revolutionary mandate of self-transformation had been reworked into a private identity even by persons targeted by the regime as potential counterrevolutionaries.

Podlubny made two holiday visits to his home village in Ukraine in 1934 and 1936. The reality he discovered there proved incompatible with his newly found aspirations as a “cultured” young man. He was appalled by the villagers’ lack of education, the prevalent patriarchal culture, and the misery of kolkhoz life. In contrast he made a point of appearing as an educated and well-dressed Muscovite to gain respect in the village. During his 1936 visit, when he was already a student, he wore fake eyeglasses to impress the villagers. Their response was mixed: young girls adored him, but there were others who complained that the kulaks had not been dealt with sufficiently at the time of dekulakization. Eventually Podlubny had to cut his visit short and escape. Friends had informed him that local authorities wanted to arrest him.

Podlubny’s posturing reveals him as a beneficiary of the Soviet system, which gave him authority, culture, and the assurance that he had emancipated himself from the idiocy of rural life. In particular his contacts with relatives and friends from his former home in Ukraine un-derscored to him that there was no viable alternative to his life in Moscow, the country’s cultural center—conditional and precarious as that life was.

children: 1933年冬天，当护照普查运动如火如荼地进行时，斯捷潘·波德卢布内去找了一位笔迹学家评估他的个人特质。对他笔迹的科学分析应该能帮助他解决那个终极问题——他是否适应苏联秩序。他把所有的积蓄，七个卢布，都花在了那次分析上，但他并不后悔这笔支出，因为他知道那位笔迹学家是该领域的最高权威，“祖耶夫-因萨罗夫本人”。几周后，他通过邮件收到了分析报告。全文引用如下，它读起来就像一份当时公开宣传的价值清单，波德卢布内的性格特质就是对照这些价值进行评估的：

一个充满主动性的人，容易掌握事物的本质。唯物主义世界观。政治导向。在很小的时候就摆脱了家庭的思想影响。具有观察天赋。能从他人的声音中辨别谎言与真诚。在他人陪伴下社交能力强且令人愉快，温柔，甚至心地善良，但当需要采取果断措施，或者必须履行某项义务或强烈的愿望时，无论是亲密朋友的恳求还是任何其他诱惑都不能使他分心，偏离他为自己设定的目标。不让自己受到任何形式的强迫。在实现意图时具有持久性，尽管他的坚持偶尔缺乏系统性和精确性：更大程度的意志集中是必不可少的。能够同时做很多事情，但有推迟已开始事情的倾向。懒惰。表现出很少的信任并疑心重，形成了职业性的谨慎。倾向于形式和逻辑推理，表现出用科学方法论处理问题的天赋，适合法律和行政领域的活动，在机械方面也有天赋。能赢得尊重。有文学天赋。天生适合各种社会工作。趋向于自我教育，尽管在这方面他应该努力深化而不是拓宽知识。在激情方面是一个伟大的实验者，偶尔表现出的好奇心多于激情，激情具有不稳定性。能够控制自己的情绪，但在释放情绪后则不行。花钱挥霍，不知道如何节俭。在危险时刻不失冷静，不为自己担心，这当然不是因为他超越了普遍的人性弱点，而仅仅是因为他相信自己的力量并保持镇定。

为波德卢布内的这一性格特征描述提供背景的模范公民，是一个具有政治倾向和唯物主义世界观的个体，他在性格中表现出坚定和果敢——“意志集中”——他对科学和进一步教育表现出兴趣，同时也是一名优秀的体力劳动者。根据祖耶夫-因萨罗夫的分析，波德卢布内在很大程度上符合这一理想。当他收到这份文件时，他对其描述的准确性印象深刻，但也感到惊讶，因为笔迹学家赋予了他许多积极的品质。具体到他的意志力，“就意志力而言，我甚至没想到我有很强的意志力。但他说我很执着。”他总结道：“这封信对我很有用。我开始了解自己，相信自己，相信我的行动和我的力量。”

In the winter of 1933, with the passport campaign in full swing, Stepan Podlubny went to a graphologist for an assessment of his personal qualities. A scientific analysis of his handwriting should help him solve the question of questions—whether he fit into the Soviet order or not. He put all of his savings, seven rubles, into that analysis, but did not regret the expenditure because he knew the graphologist to be the greatest authority in the field, “Zuev-Insarov himself.” Several weeks later he received his analysis in the mail. Quoted in full, it reads like a catalogue of publicly proclaimed values of the time, against which Podlubny’s personality traits are assessed:

A personality full of initiative, who easily grasps the essence of a matter. Materialistic worldview. Politically oriented. Escaped the ideological influence of his family at an early age. Has a gift for observation. Can distinguish lies from sincerity in the voice of another person. In the company of others is sociable and pleasant, gentle, even good-natured, but when decisive measures are called for, or when an obligation or a strong desire has to be fulfilled, neither the pleas of close friends nor any other temptations can distract him from the goal he has set himself. Does not let himself be coerced in any fashion. Persistent in the realization of his intentions, although his perseverance is occasionally unsystematic and lacks precision: greater concentration of will is indispensable. Able to do many things at once, but has a tendency to defer things already started. Lazy. Shows little trust and is suspicious, has developed professional caution. A tendency for formal and logical reasoning, shows talent for treating issues with a scientific methodology, suited for activities in law and administration, is also mechanically talented. Can command respect. Has a literary vein. By nature suited to all varieties of social work. Gravitates toward self-education, although in this regard he should strive for a deepening, rather than broadening, of his knowledge. A great experimenter in terms of his passions, occasionally displays more curiosity than passion, inconstancy in his passions. Able to control his emotions, but not after releasing them. Extravagant with money, and does not know how to economize. Does not lose his head in moments of danger, does not fear for himself, not because, of course, he stands above universal human weaknesses, but simply because he believes in his strength and maintains a presence of mind.

The model citizen who provided the background to this characterization of Podlubny was a politically inclined individual with a materialistic worldview, who in his character displayed firmness and determination—“concentration of will”—who expressed interest in science and in furthering his education, but who was also a good manual worker. For the most part Podlubny lived up to the ideal, according to ZuevInsarov’s analysis. When he received the document, he was impressed with how accurately he had been characterized, but was also surprised that the graphologist had assigned to him many positive qualities. Specifically with respect to his willpower, “as far as willpower is concerned, I didn’t even expect that I have strong willpower. But he says that I’m persistent.” He concluded: “The letter was useful for me. I’ve begun to know myself, to trust myself, to trust my actions and my strength.”

波德卢布内对他的意志力十分着迷。在他的理解中，意志和意识是相互依存的；没有一个就无法获得另一个。这种联系在他将工作表现的退步以及他“白痴且非政治的情绪”归咎于“意志薄弱”的日记条目中显而易见。但意志力不仅要赋予一个好的苏联公民以发达的政治意识，还要帮助他保守社会背景和他内心深处“黑暗”思想的双重秘密。只有通过“意志”、“决心”和“冷静”，他才能将私人想法与公共行为隔绝开来。相当矛盾的是，坚强的意志同时帮助他成为苏联秩序的一员，并作为受威胁物种的伪装成员适应它。

波德卢布内指出，生活意味着斗争，在多个“战线”上持续不断地斗争。他曾将自己比作大海上的孤独水手，面临着突然爆发的可怕风暴。在一个压倒性的力量随时可能摧毁他的环境中生存的唯一方法，就是听从他的“本能”并制定“自我保护计划”。波德卢布内反复提醒自己，要为来自任何方向的迫在眉睫的打击做好准备。他尤其怀疑平静时期，当似乎没有任何东西威胁他时，无论是在工作单位还是来自格别乌。这些时期让他想起“暴风雨前的宁静”。斗争是生活中不可避免的事实，但也包含道德价值，因为正是在斗争中，一个人在身体和情感意义上都变得更坚韧、更强大。如果没有需要克服的障碍，意志就会退化，腐蚀自我，并破坏其在日常生活的“生存斗争”中的适应能力。“没有斗争的生活是单调的，也是未来的坏兆头。”

如果说意志力是社会主义社会自我发展的关键要素，那么它也是波德卢布内认为区分苏联社会阶级的标准。他认为拥有巨大意志力并因此能够应对苏联生活条件的人是“无产阶级”。斯捷潘在描述他母亲避开无所不在的警察监视的机智时，赞扬了她的意志力，并称她的态度在精神上是“纯粹无产阶级的”。这是对无产阶级行为的一种矛盾理解，因为它意味着有能力保护自己不受无产阶级国家的侵害。相比之下，他对他父亲的主要指控是，菲利普是一个“可怜的生物”，无法为自己站出来参与那种定义了无产阶级、甚至是人类（相对于纯粹动物般的生存）的斗争。

Podlubny obsessed about his willpower. In his understanding, will and consciousness were interdependent; one could not be attained without the other. This link becomes evident in entries in which he blamed his “weak will” for setbacks in his work performance and for his “idiotic and nonpolitical mood.” But willpower was not only to impart the developed political consciousness of a good Soviet citizen, it also helped him preserve the double secret of his social background and his innermost “black” thoughts. Only through “will,” “determination,” and “cold-bloodedness” could he seal off his private thoughts from his behavior in public. Quite paradoxically, a strong will helped him at one and the same time become a member of the Soviet order and adapt to it as a disguised member of an imperiled species.

To live, Podlubny noted, meant to struggle, continuously and on multiple “fronts.” He once likened himself to a lonely sailor on the ocean, facing the sudden outbreak of a terrible storm. The only way to survive in an environment whose overwhelming forces could destroy him at any moment was to listen to his “instincts” and develop a “plan of self-preservation.” Repeatedly Podlubny reminded himself to be prepared for imminent blows from any direction. He was especially suspicious about calm periods, when nothing seemed to threaten him, neither at work nor from the GPU. They reminded him of the “calm before the storm.” Struggle was an unavoidable fact of life, but it also contained moral value, for it was in struggle that one became tougher and stronger, in both a physical and an emotional sense. If there were no obstacles to overcome, the will regressed, corrupting the self and undermining its fitness in the “survival struggle” of daily life. “A life without struggle is monotonous and a bad omen for the future.”

If willpower was the key element necessary for self-development in socialist society, it was also what Podlubny thought distinguished the classes in Soviet society. He considered to be “proletarian” someone who possessed great willpower and therefore could cope with the conditions of Soviet life. Describing the resourcefulness of his mother, as she eluded the watchful gaze of the omnipresent police, Stepan praised her willpower and described her attitude as “purely proletarian” in spirit. It was a paradoxical understanding of proletarian behavior, since it connoted the ability to protect oneself against the proletarian state. By contrast his main charge against the father was that Filip, a “pathetic creature,” was unable to stand up for himself and engage in the type of struggle that defined a proletarian and, indeed, a human being, in opposition to mere animal-like existence.

在这一逻辑令人不安的延伸中，波德卢布内将社会中那些无法应对苏联环境的群体定义为“意志薄弱”且不适合生存。1933年冬天，他和母亲收到了来自旧家的信。这是斯捷潘的姨妈丽莎维塔（他母亲的姐姐）的三个年幼孩子的绝望求救。丽莎维塔是个寡妇，因为从集体农庄偷拿粮食喂养饥饿的家人而入狱。她根据斯大林的“五穗法”被判刑，该法律对“盗窃社会主义财产”规定了严厉的惩罚。孩子们写道：“弗罗西娅姨妈和斯秋帕哥哥！我们饿得全身浮肿，如果可以的话，请救救我们。如果不行就别救了，反正我们迟早都要死的。但我们想再活一会儿，我们的生命太短暂了。”当他的母亲“痛哭流涕”时，斯捷潘强调了自己的“冷静”行为。他补充说，“出于某种原因”，读这封信让他露出了微笑。波德卢布内在同年夏天更充分地阐述了他对乌克兰饥饿同胞的态度。他的母亲前往家乡别廖佐夫卡村，带着饥荒的恐怖景象回来：
一半的人死于饥饿。现在他们吃煮熟的甜菜叶。发生了许多人食人的案例……总而言之，正在发生的事情很可怕。我不知道为什么，但我对此并不感到同情。事情必须这样，因为只有这样才更容易将农民的小私有者心理重塑为我们需要的无产阶级心理。而那些死于饥饿的人，就让他们死吧。如果他们不能保护自己免于饿死，这意味着他们意志薄弱，他们能给社会带来什么呢？

In an unnerving extension of this logic, Podlubny defined those groups in society who could not cope with the Soviet environment as “weak-willed” and unfit for life. In the winter of 1933 he and his mother received a letter from their former home. It was a desperate cry for help from the three small children of Stepan’s aunt Lisaveta, his mother’s older sister. A widow, Lisaveta was in prison for having picked grain from the collective farm to feed her starving family. She was sentenced under Stalin’s “five wheat-ear law,” which imposed harsh punishment for the “theft of socialist property.” The children wrote: “Aunt Frosya and brother Styopa! We are bloated from hunger, help us, if you can. Do not if you can’t, we will have to die sooner or later anyway. But we want to live a little longer, our lives have been so short.” While his mother “cried bitter tears,” Stepan emphasized his own “cool” behavior. “For some reason,” he added, reading the letter made him smile. Podlubny articulated his attitude toward his starving brethren in Ukraine more fully in the summer of the same year. His mother had traveled to their home village of Beryozovka, and she returned with horrifying images of the famine:

Half of the people have died of hunger. Now they are eating boiled beet tops. There are numerous cases of cannibalism . . . All in all, what’s happening is awful. I don’t know why, but I don’t feel sympathy for this. It has to be this way, because then it will be easier to remake the peasants’ smallholder psychology into the proletarian psychology that we need. And those who die of hunger, let them die. If they can’t defend themselves against death from starvation, it means that they are weak-willed, and what can they give to society?

波德卢布内提出的这种令人震惊的功利主义哲学，与布尔什维克国家宣扬的革命道德有关，但在重要方面又有所不同。波德卢布内一直援引布尔什维克人格的性格特征和范畴，如意志力和自我控制，但他这样做不仅是为了表达自我，也是为了在严酷的共产主义世界中生存下去，为了以伪装的阶级敌人的身份保护自己。他从“现实生活”和他人的行为中获得启示，很少援引理论或历史作为他个人生活的指南。他是一个公开的宿命论者，表达了一种与他的生活经验相符的信念：存在着超出他意志的力量，随时可能重塑他的生活。波德卢布内知道，这种对命运的信仰更多是传统农民的特征，而不是一个开明的现代公民的特征，但他依然依赖它。此外，他听从“本能”的声音，这与共产党人截然不同，后者鄙视无组织、前人类的潜意识，崇拜发达理性的力量。

波德卢布内贴切地将自己的处境描述为一只“小动物”，只能依靠本能和模仿能力在掠食性的世界中生存。在内务人民委员部（NKVD）揭穿波德卢布内身份的过程中，这种自我构想以近乎滑稽的方式表现出来。当官员们追问他为什么以前没有向他们坦白自己的真实出身时，他只说了一句：“小鸡也想活下去。”这是当时流行的一首源于俄罗斯监狱文化的歌曲中的台词，歌中一只“又煮又炸的小鸡”走在圣彼得堡的涅夫斯基大街上，因为没有护照被警察逮捕。
波德卢布内认为，只有像他这样的阶级异己，才过着小鸡一样不稳定的生活。这种生存模式只在他处于社会非法地位期间适用。一旦他跨越鸿沟走向合法地位，他就能毫无保留地向高尔基和那个时代其他作家所倡导的、拥有完整世界观的坚强且不受束缚的人格理想靠拢。

The shockingly utilitarian philosophy propounded by Podlubny was related to the revolutionary morality preached by the Bolshevik state but differed from it in significant respects. Podlubny consistently invoked character traits and categories of the Bolshevik personality such as willpower and self-control, yet he did so not only to express himself but also merely to survive in the harsh Communist world, to protect himself as a class enemy in disguise. He took his cues from “real life” and the behavior of others, rarely invoking theory or history as a guide to his personal life. He was an avowed believer in fate, expressing a conviction, consistent with his life experience, that there were forces beyond his volition that could reshape his life at any moment. Podlubny knew that such belief in fate was more characteristic of the traditional peasantry than of an enlightened, modern citizen, but he relied on it nonetheless. Moreover, he listened to the voice of his “in-stincts,” a stark difference from Communists, who looked down on the disorganized, prehuman unconscious and worshipped the powers of developed reason.

Fittingly Podlubny described his plight as that of a “small animal” with only its instincts and powers of mimicry to rely on for survival in a predatory world. In almost comical ways this self-conception came to the fore during Podlubny’s unmasking by the NKVD. When the officers prodded him about why he had not confided his true origins to them before, all he said was: “The little chicken also wants to live.” It was a line from a popular song coming out of Russian prison culture, in which a “boiled and fried chicken” walks on St. Petersburg’s Nevsky Prospekt and is arrested by the police because it does not have a passport.

Only class aliens like him, Podlubny believed, lived the precarious existence of the small chicken. This survivalist mode applied only for the duration of his illegal standing in society. As soon as he crossed the gap toward legality he would be able to orient himself unconditionally toward the ideal, propounded by Gorky and other writers of the age, of the strong and unfettered personality with an integrated worldview.

children: 1934年12月1日，被广泛视为斯大林第一副手的列宁格勒党书记谢尔盖·基洛夫被谋杀。党的领导层对此感到愤怒，要求无情迫害被怀疑来自政治反对派的谋杀者。基洛夫谋杀案是布尔什维克体制历史上的一个转折点：它重新定向了净化运动，此前该运动的目标是阶级异己、资本主义剥削者和资产阶级民族主义者，现在则转向党内，最终导致了1937年和1938年数十万共产党员被捕和被处决。谋杀发生的时间也标志着波德卢布内生活的转折点。他对自己的看法以及他写日记的风格都发生了显著而持久的变化。这种变化与他意识到自己似乎无法摆脱那些与苏联政权目标格格不入的性格特征有关。

On December 1, 1934, the Leningrad party secretary, Sergei Kirov, widely regarded as Stalin’s first deputy, was murdered. The party leadership reacted with outrage, demanding relentless persecution of the murderers, who were suspected to come from the political opposition. The Kirov murder was a turning point in the history of the Bolshevik system: it redirected the purge campaign, which up to then had targeted class aliens, capitalist exploiters, and bourgeois nationalists, toward the party itself, culminating in the arrests and executions of hundreds of thousands of Communists in 1937 and 1938. The time of the murder also marked a turning point in Podlubny’s life. His view of himself, as well as the style in which he kept his diary notes, underwent a notable and lasting change. This change was connected to his realization that he appeared unable to part with character traits that were alien to the goals of the Soviet regime.

波德卢布内在1933年就已经发现了这一点，当时他与同事米佳·戈连科夫进行了一系列非法的政治谈话。戈连科夫一直向他朗诵诗歌和其他作品，诉说着个人的不幸和生活的艰辛。这些谈话让波德卢布内深感矛盾。米佳的想法引起了他自己某些感受的共鸣，而且米佳能说出这些感受，满足了他对日记之外“灵魂伴侣”的渴求。此外，与米佳的谈话让他瞥见了一个“非正统”的、“深刻”的人，这个人有“自己的见解”，并且不怕表达出来——这与那些志在晋升、肤浅且盲目附和上级“旨意”的“国家传声筒”形成了鲜明对比。然而，斯捷潘又忍不住将米佳对政治秩序的批评定性为“悲观主义”和小资产阶级，因为这与作为备受推崇的社会主义人格核心的乐观、自信和果敢相冲突。斯捷潘发现听到米佳计划写一部关于“悲观与进步青年”的小说让他感到“不愉快”，米佳想以自己和斯捷潘为原型创作“悲观”角色，而另一个朋友则是“进步”型的灵感来源。斯捷潘显然更愿意被归入乐观主义者之列。

波德卢布内通过阐述他内心有两个人的方式来理解他的内心冲突：“其中一个是官僚，他每天提醒我：保持警惕，遵守规则，非常小心，不要信口开河，注意你自己和你所说的话！他总是给我指示。这个人大部分时间都活在我体内。第二个人，他是在我灵魂里收集各种污垢、所有剩余垃圾的人，他等待合适的时机将这些臭气熏天的脏东西倒在别人头上，以减轻自己身上的负担。这个人在我体内出现的次数较少，但他确实存在。”他补充说，第二个人是“我出身的旧伤和记忆”的结果。波德卢布内相信，只要他成为苏联社会的合法成员，他就能拥有那种具备单一、整合的世界观的理想人格。

Podlubny had already made this discovery in 1933, during a series of illicit political conversations with a friend at work, Mitya Gorenkov. Gorenkov had been reciting to him poems and other writings that bespoke his personal unhappiness and the hardships of life. The conversations left Podlubny profoundly ambivalent. Mitya’s thoughts echoed some of his own feelings, and the ability to voice them satisfied his craving for a “soul mate” beyond the diary. Moreover, the conversations with Mitya gave him a glimpse of an “unorthodox,” “deep” person who had an “own opinion” and was not afraid of voicing it—in contrast to the career-minded “state parrots,” who were shallow and mindlessly echoed what was “dictated” to them. Yet at the same time, Stepan could not help characterizing Mitya’s critique of the political order as “pessimist” and petit-bourgeois, given that it clashed with the cheerful confidence, optimism, and resolve that were at the core of the extolled socialist personality. Stepan found it “unpleasant” to hear that Mitya planned to write a novel on “pessimistic and progressive youth,” and wanted to base the “pessimist” characters on himself and Stepan, while another friend was to serve as inspiration for the “progressive” type. Stepan clearly preferred to be counted among the optimists.

Podlubny made sense of his inner conflict by stating that there were two people inside him: “One of them is a bureaucrat who reminds me every day: stay on your guard, observe the rules, be very careful, don’t talk through your hat, watch yourself and what you’re saying! He always gives me instructions. This person lives in me most of the time. The second person, he’s someone who collects all sorts of dirt in my soul, all the leftover garbage, and he waits for the right moment to pour this stinking mess over someone else’s head to relieve himself from the burden of this dirt. This person is less present in me, but he exists.” The second person, he added, was an effect of the “old wound of my origins and memories.” Podlubny believed that the ideal type of personality, endowed with a single, integrated worldview, would be within his reach as soon as he became a legal member of Soviet society.
然而，就在他诊断出体内有两个人的几天后，内务部对他身份的揭穿不仅粉碎了他合法化的希望，而且使他一直试图摆脱的阶级异己身份变得本质化了：
在与我的每一次谈话中，他们（他的联络员）都提醒我的过去，强迫我，向我灌输一切不必要的东西。以前我不去想我的过去，我是社会中普通的一员，我甚至还在先锋队里。但现在他们，正是他们自己，强迫我以不同的方式思考。然后他们会为此打击我，毫无疑问，当他们发现时，他们会打击我。这太可怕了，正在发生的事情太可怕了。他们没有治愈我，反而把我变成了一个残废。

Yet his unmasking by the NVKD, only days after he diagnosed the two people within him, not only dashed his hope for legalization but essentialized the very identity as a class alien from which he had sought to absolve himself all along:

In every conversation with me they [his contact officers] remind me of my past, forcing me, inculcating everything unnecessary in me. Previously I didn’t think about my past, I was an ordinary rank-and-file member of society, I was even in the vanguard. But now they, they themselves, have forced me to think differently. Then they will beat me for this, and there’s no doubt that when they find out, they’ll beat me. It’s so horrible, horrible what is happening. Instead of curing me, they are making a cripple of me.

波德卢布内特别指责内务部在他身上灌输了全新的、完全“不必要”的想法，公然违背了他们作为营救道德危机中苏联公民的精神医生的职责。这些新想法非常引人注目：1935年1月，听到另一位政治家瓦列里安·古比雪夫据说死于心脏病的消息，波德卢布内怀疑古比雪夫是根据政府命令被杀的，也许是因为他预定在政府代表大会上发表的讲话批评性太强，“所以他们决定除掉他”。他不相信官方的死亡报告，“就像不相信一个以前偷过东西的小偷一样”——这是暗指上个月的“基洛夫谋杀案闹剧”。然而，在表达这些尖锐观点的同时，波德卢布内也对自己提出了严厉指责，责备自己视角“太现实”。他不再是“进步”苏联青年的一员；他的“意识形态”已经“腐烂”了。

Podlubny specifically blamed the NKVD for instilling in him new and wholly “unnecessary” thoughts, in blatant violation of their vocation as spiritual doctors who were to rescue Soviet citizens in moral crisis. These new thoughts were remarkable: in January 1935, hearing of the death of another politician, Valerian Kuibyshev, who was said to have died of a heart attack, Podlubny suspected that Kuibyshev had been killed on the government’s orders, perhaps because the speech he was scheduled to deliver at a government congress was too critical and “so they decided to get him out of the way.” He distrusted the official death report, “just the way one distrusts a thief who had stolen before”—a reference to the “comedy of the Kirov murder” the previous month. Yet while voicing these stark opinions, Podlubny also leveled serious accusations against himself, chiding himself for his “too realistic” perspective. No longer was he a member of “progressive” Soviet youth; his “ideology” had become “rotten.”

长远来看，他有两种可能的方式来面对自己的“反动”立场。一种是重新调整自我定义的范畴，使他的非法想法看起来合法。如果无法重新塑造自己眼中的世界，他便势必使自己边缘化：接受自己的想法偏离了规范，并在自己身上寻找偏离的原因。波德卢布内同时参与了这两个过程。他的日记说明了他如何设法重新排列他的政治词汇。在1935年2月的一篇条目中，他描述了对基洛夫杀手及其党羽日益扩大的搜捕：“反动和迫害的时代已经到来……几句话无法描述。它只让我想起学习1907年的党史：一场肆虐的黑色反动，正在发生。一场肆虐的反动，以及对思想自由的迫害。”
这些句子使波德卢布内能够通过将政权定义为反动，并含蓄地将自己描绘成“进步”，从而摆脱他的“反动”想法。更令人震惊的是波德卢布内对激发这种新观念并促使他谴责党国的来源的引用：布尔什维克党的历史教科书。这就好像他用《圣经》对抗教会，以使其不信显得合法。他援引官方的苏联话语来破坏现存政治政权的合法性。但与此同时，这一立场巩固了他与政治政权共享的革命行动主义这一共同的苏联立场。

In the long run, two possibilities were available to him to accommodate his “reactionary” stance. One was to rearrange the categories of self-definition, so that his illegitimate thoughts would appear legitimate. If he proved unable to remake the world for himself, he was bound to marginalize himself: to accept his individual thoughts as a deviation from the norm and to seek the reasons for the deviation in himself. Podlubny engaged in both processes. His diary illustrates the ways in which he managed to rearrange his political vocabulary. In an entry of February 1935 he described the widening hunt for Kirov’s murderers and their henchmen: “A time of reaction and persecution has set in . . . You can’t describe it in a few words. It only reminds me of studying the history of the party in 1907: a raging black reaction, going on right now. A raging reaction, and the persecution of free thought.”

These sentences enabled Podlubny to rid himself of his “reactionary” thoughts by defining the regime as reactionary and, by implication, portraying himself as “progressive.” Even more striking is Podlubny’s reference to the source that inspired this new conceptualization, and that brought him to denounce the party state: the Bolshevik party’s history textbook. It was as if he used the Bible against the Church in legitimizing his unbelief. He invoked official Soviet discourse to undermine the legitimacy of the existing political regime. But at the same time, this stance cemented the Soviet platform of revolutionary activism that he shared with the political regime.

波德卢布内意识到他的批评对他作为苏联社会主体所受到的不利影响。既然他作为一个苏联公民的主体性是由革命提供的参数——行动主义、热情、服从集体、对工人国家的忠诚——定义的，他开始将自己对国家政策的批评视为个人堕落的过程。他注意到他的新人生观，由于缺乏振奋人心的想法，“在道德上麻痹了”他，使他感到“迟钝”，仿佛患上了“严重的内心疾病”。与此前哀叹自己意志薄弱时不同，他这一次对自己的“病”是否能够治愈更加不确定。他是一个只是暂时屈服于腐败影响的好苏联公民，还是他在本质上就与苏联价值观格格不入？
波德卢布内反复将自己称为一个无药可救的人，被他的出身和教养不可逆转地塑造了。如果一个人的意识决定了他的阶级地位，那么波德卢布内将他持久的异端思想倾向视为异己阶级本质的表现也就顺理成章了。
在从灵魂状态推断自己的社会阶级身份时，他遵循了1930年代公共领域中无数人实践的模式。通过告发和审判，政治嫌疑人的传记被有系统地重写。因此，莫斯科大审判中的被告——大部分是坚定的老布尔什维克——被国家公诉机关重新塑造成反动的白卫军分子、资本主义间谍或帝国主义势力的雇佣兵。然而，波德卢布内在他的秘密日记中上演了一场针对自己的审判。

Podlubny was aware of the deleterious impact of his criticism on himself as a subject of the Soviet realm. Since his subjectivity as a Soviet citizen was defined by parameters supplied by the revolution—activism, enthusiasm, subordination to the collective, loyalty toward the workers’ state—he came to regard his criticism of state policies as a process of personal degeneration. He noted that his new view on life, bereft as it was of uplifting thoughts, “paralyzed” him “morally” and made him feel “sluggish,” as if he suffered from a “grave inner disease.” What distinguished this from previous situations in which he had lamented the weakness of his will was his greater uncertainty as to whether his “sickness” could be cured. Was he a good Soviet citizen who had only temporarily succumbed to a corrupting influence, or was he alien to Soviet values in his very essence?

Repeatedly Podlubny referred to himself as a person beyond help, irreversibly shaped by his origins and upbringing. If an individual’s consciousness determined his class position, it only made sense that Podlubny regarded his persistent proclivity toward heretical thought as an expression of an alien class essence.

In deducing his social class identity from the state of his soul, he followed a scheme practiced by countless others in the public sphere of the 1930s. By means of denunciations and trials, the biographies of politically suspect people were systematically rewritten. Thus the defendants at the Moscow show trials—for the most part staunch Old Bolsheviks—were reconfigured by the state prosecution into reactionary White Guardists, capitalist spies, or mercenaries of imperialist powers. Yet Podlubny staged a trial against himself, and did so in his secret diary.

波德卢布内不仅评估他自己的想法和行为，还评估他人的想法和行为，将其视为社会背景的表现。他曾将自己与另一个富农之子进行比较，指出两人拥有相同的“心理”，这在他们不稳定的爱情生活中表现出来：“既然我们两人的出身相同，我得出结论，这种现象存在于所有受过类似教育的人身上，存在于所有走过这条人生道路的人身上。”他曾偷看了一位来访的朋友奥列格·瓦赫纳泽的日记。他读到的内容让他怀疑瓦赫纳泽是“贵族的儿子，根本不是他所说的那样……他的父亲还活着，住在国外。当我分析他的冒险经历，回忆他的脾气和恶作剧时，我的怀疑进一步加深了。这个庸人的知识分子恶作剧，他对香粉的热爱，他优雅的举止和文雅的言谈，他完全的疲惫和薄弱的意志力——所有这些特质，当我的过去沉重地压在身上、当我不得安宁时，我都能在自己身上注意到。我在他身上找到了所有这些特质。”
一个人的性格，特别是意志力的发展，波德卢布内暗示，是由社会背景决定的，以至于个人性格带有某种生物决定论的意味。苏联政权对社会出身的强调，就像在波德卢布内的案例中一样，可能导致个体出身被当作本质，而个人行为反被忽略。

Podlubny evaluated not only his own thoughts and behavior but also those of other people as expressions of sociological background. He once compared himself to another son of a kulak, noting that both shared the same “psychology,” revealed in their unsteady love lives: “Since we both have the same origins, I concluded that this phenomenon exists with all people who had a similar education, with everybody who has traveled this path in life.” He once secretly read the diary of a visiting friend, Oleg Vachnadze. What he read made him suspect that Vachnadze was the “son of a nobleman and not at all what he says . . . His father is alive and lives abroad. When I analyze his adventures, and recall his tempers and pranks, my suspicion is hardened further. These intelligentsia pranks of a philistine, his love of powder, the elegance of his manners and his polished speech, his total exhaustion and feeble willpower—all of these things I notice in myself when my past is weighing on me, when I’m not left in peace. I find all these traits in him.”

A person’s character and in particular the development of his or her willpower, Podlubny implied, was determined by social background, so much so that personal character acquired a degree of biological determinism. The Soviet regime’s strong emphasis on social origins could, as in Podlubny’s case, lead to an essentialization of individuals’ origins at the expense of their deeds.

1936年初，波德卢布内的富农出身在一次共青团会议上被公开揭露，他被开除出青年组织。他在日记中报告了自己对这一事件的震惊，但也描述了自己在会议上表现得多么大胆。他直视着每个人的眼睛，“甚至［忘了］好好忏悔我的罪过”。他特别对官方对他的指控提出了异议，辩称他父亲的家产并不符合富农农庄的规模。它更像是一个“大型中农农庄”。波德卢布内报告说，这一说法为他赢得了一次针对反苏行为的官方申诫：“从我关于家产的话中，他们得出结论，我反对对我父亲的去富农化处理，尽管我多次声明我没说过这种话。”波德卢布内在演讲结束时宣称：“如果你们想，尽管把我开除出共青团。但至于学院，我会为我的权利而战。”在援引他的“权利”时，波德卢布内指的是1935年12月最近的政府法令，该法令取消了对阶级异己背景人员的大学入学限制。
为了应对被医学院开除的威胁，波德卢布内决定绘制一份家谱。他相信，这份文件迟早会在他与当局的冲突中派上用场。在父母和一位同样住在莫斯科的堂表亲的帮助下，波德卢布内重建了他父亲的族谱，始于18世纪的曾曾祖父米龙。这份家谱是为了帮助他证明，他父亲家族的许多成员，包括他的父亲本人，并不是该被打上“富农”标签的进取资本家。

但追踪家谱的行为本身就表明，波德卢布内早先那种认为阶级成员身份是自觉选择的结果的理想主义期待，在多大程度上受到生物决定论观念的制约。他对他家族过去四代人的社会经济命运的回顾，说明了他相信理解他主体性的一个重要钥匙在于他的家庭背景以及它调节他“心理”的方式，而不是在于个人行为和重塑自我的能力。这种定义阶级身份的生物学方法在斯大林体制中流传甚广，甚至在1930年代中期宣布社会主义已建成、苏联社会已据称解决了所有阶级对抗之后依然如此。在1941年的第十八次党代表会议上，政治局委员格奥尔基·马林科夫抨击了这种对个体的谱系学理解。他宣称，党和国家官员详细审查候选人的家谱，询问他的“爷爷和他的奶奶”，却忽视他的个人品质，这是不可接受的。

波德卢布内被允许留在学院，但他医学院前两个学期的成绩非常糟糕，以至于他申请并获准休学一年，之后他计划作为一年级新生重新入学。与此同时，他的父母在1934年和1935年多次收到民兵的传唤，被迫上交证件，并被命令离开莫斯科及周边100公里半径。波德卢布内的父亲搬到了伏尔加河畔的雅罗斯拉夫尔，而他的母亲则前往半径之外的莫扎伊斯克市。在儿子的帮助下，她写信请求恢复她的全部公民权利。她于1936年12月获准返回莫斯科。

In early 1936 Podlubny’s kulak origins were publicly revealed at a Komsomol meeting and he was expelled from the youth organization. To the diary he reported how stunned he had been by this event, but also how daringly he had comported himself at the meeting. He had looked everybody straight in the eyes and “even [forgotten] to repent for my sins in a major way.” In particular he took issue with the official charge against him, contending that his father’s household had not been the size of a kulak farm. It had rather been a “large middle-peasant’s farm.” This statement, Podlubny reported, earned him an official reprimand for anti-Soviet behavior: “From my words regarding the household they concluded that I was against my father’s dekulakization, although I stated more than once that I had not said this.” Podlubny concluded his speech by declaring: “Feel free to expel me from the Komsomol if you want. But as far as the institute is concerned I will fight for my rights.” In invoking his “rights,” Podlubny was referring to the recent government decree of December 1935 that had removed the restrictions on university admission for persons of class-alien background.

To counteract the threat of being excluded from the Medical Institute, Podlubny resolved to draw up a family tree. Sooner or later, he believed, this document would prove useful in his conflict with the authorities. Together with his parents and a cousin who was also living in Moscow, Podlubny reconstructed his father’s genealogy, starting in the eighteenth century with his great-great-grandfather Miron. The family tree was to help him demonstrate that many members of his father’s family, including his father himself, had not been enterprising capitalists deserving the label “kulak.”

But the very act of tracing his genealogy suggests how much Podlubny’s earlier idealistic expectation that class membership was a matter of conscious choice had been qualified by a notion of biological determinism. His rehearsal of the socioeconomic fortunes of his family’s past four generations illustrated a belief that an important key to his subjectivity lay in his family background and the way it had conditioned his “psychology,” rather than in personal deeds and the ability to remake himself. This biological approach to defining class identity was widespread in the Stalinist system even after the mid-1930s, when socialism was declared to be built and all class antagonisms had allegedly been resolved in Soviet society. At the Eighteenth Party Conference in 1941, the Politburo member Georgy Malenkov attacked this genealogical understanding of individuals. It was inadmissible, he declared, for party and state officials to sift through a candidate’s family tree and ask him about his “grandfather and his grandmother,” yet to ignore his personal qualities.

Podlubny was allowed to remain in the institute, but his performance in the first two semesters of his medical studies had been so poor that he applied for, and was granted, a year-long leave, after which he planned to enroll again as a first-year student. Meanwhile, his parents, who had repeatedly received citations from the militia in 1934 and 1935, were forced to surrender their documents and ordered to leave Moscow and the surrounding 100 kilometer radius. Podlubny’s father moved to Yaroslavl on the Volga, while his mother traveled to the city of Mozhaisk, just outside the radius. Helped by her son, she wrote petitions pleading for the restoration of her full civic rights. She was allowed to return to Moscow in December 1936.

波德卢布内的日记在1936年12月下旬中断，直到1937年12月才恢复。在那一年的第一篇条目中，他解释了中断的原因：过去的一年太可怕了，他想把它划掉，就像他生命史中“不必要的一页”。他提到了因失去奖学金而产生的经济困难。他长达一年的休学导致他失去了学院里的朋友。最后，他担心可能因为成绩不及格和需要赚钱而不得不退学。一旦波德卢布内的自我改造项目（无论是物质上的还是道德上的）看起来不再可行，他的日记就沉寂了。在谈到他在1937年的生活时，他提到了死尸下凝结的一滩血，以及他感到勒在脖子上的绞索正在收紧。这些无疑是对他周围政治暴力以及他可能成为其目标的威胁的影射。

虽然斯大林在1936年至1938年的大清洗旨在清除国家和党政机构中可疑的反对派，但许多既不是共产党员也不是高级国家管理人员的人也沦为受害者。“富农、土匪和其他反苏分子”是1937年7月31日发布的内务部第447号命令的目标群体，该命令导致了数十万人的逮捕和处决。命令为该国每个地区设定了逮捕配额。仅在莫斯科地区，就要处决5000名反苏分子，另外3万名要被判处8到10年的劳改。在接下来的几个月里，随着发现更多的敌人，地区内务部领导人请求政治局提高配额；他们的请求得到了批准。
通过审查有阶级异己或政治反革命记录者的档案，这些惊人的配额便能在社会主义竞赛的精神下得到完成，甚至超额完成。

Podlubny’s diary breaks off in late December 1936, resuming only in December 1937. In the first entry of that year, he explained the hiatus: the past year had been so appalling that he wanted to cross it out, “like an unnecessary page” in the history of his life. He mentioned financial troubles stemming from the loss of his scholarship. His year-long leave had led to the loss of friends from the institute. Finally there was the fear that he might have to quit the institute because of his failing grades and the need to earn money. Podlubny’s diary fell silent as soon as his project of self-transformation, material and moral, appeared no longer viable. In talking about his life in 1937, he referred to a puddle of blood congealing under a dead body, and to a noose that he felt tightening around his neck. These were certainly references to the political violence around him and the threat that he might become its target.

While Stalin’s Great Purges of 1936–1938 aimed at cleansing the state and party administration of suspected oppositionists, scores of people who were neither Communists nor top state managers fell victim to them as well. “Kulaks, bandits, and other anti-Soviet elements” were the target group of NKVD order no. 447, issued on July 31, 1937, which produced arrests and executions in the hundreds of thousands. The order set arrest quotas for each of the country’s regions. In the Moscow region alone five thousand anti-Soviet elements were to be executed and another thirty thousand sentenced to labor camps for eight to ten years. Over the next months regional NKVD leaders petitioned the Politburo to raise the quotas, as more enemies had been identified; their requests were granted.
These staggering quotas could be met and exceeded in the spirit of socialist competition through examination of the files of people with a record as class aliens or political counterrevolutionaries.
波德卢布内并没有被告知这项秘密行动，他依靠他所信赖的直觉和实践经验来保护自己和母亲。他描述的不断收紧的绞索是指即将于1937年12月12日举行的苏联最高苏维埃选举。根据以往的经验，波德卢布内知道警察习惯在重大节日的前夕进行突击搜查。因为逮捕总是在夜间发生，他和母亲考虑在朋友家住几晚，但最后他们并没有这样做。

Podlubny, who was not informed of this secret operation, relied on his trusted instruments of intuition and practical experience to protect himself and his mother. The tightening noose he described referred to the approaching elections to the USSR’s Supreme Soviet, to be held on December 12, 1937. From past experience Podlubny knew that the police habitually conducted raids on the eve of major holidays. Because arrests always happened at night, he and his mother considered staying with friends for a few nights, but in the end they did not do so.

不过，波德卢布内确实采取了一项预防措施：他把日记藏在他们公共公寓走廊里的一个大箱子里，就在他和母亲住的房间外面。12月9日凌晨4点，他们被可怕的敲门声惊醒。一名持枪的刑事警察在看门人的陪同下要求进入他们的房间并进行了搜查，波德卢布内猜测他搜查的显然是武器。在记录下搜查一无所获后，警察要求斯捷潘的母亲穿好衣服陪他去警察局“待一会儿”。那天晚上她没有回来。

Podlubny did take one precaution, however: he hid his diary in a trunk in the corridor of their communal apartment, outside the room where he and his mother lived. At 4 a.m. on December 9 they were awakened by the dreaded knock at their door. An armed officer of the criminal police, accompanied by a janitor, demanded entry to their room and searched it, apparently for weapons, Podlubny suspected. After making a note that the search had yielded nothing, the officer asked Stepan’s mother to get dressed and accompany him to the police station “for just a minute.” She did not return that night.

在斯捷潘·波德卢布内对逮捕的反应中，他对母亲非同寻常的依恋显露无遗。在接下来的几天和几周里，他一直在寻找她。每天早上，莫斯科民兵的问讯处都会排起长队。为了在下午4点关闭前赶到问讯窗口，他必须在凌晨5点后不久到达那里。站在长达半公里的队伍中，看着数百名寻找被捕亲友的莫斯科人，他发现了一个对官方世界的指令和陈词滥调浑然不觉的人群世界：他们“沉浸在自己的私人事务中，对他们来说，外部世界并不存在”。然后轮到他在那个小方窗前了：“一种无法解释的恐惧向我袭来。我的膝盖发抖下陷，手指神经质地颤抖。心跳加速……直到回家后，我才充分意识到发生的事情的意义。喉头哽住了，几乎喘不过气来。我失去了对肌肉的控制。”窗口的官员无法告诉他母亲在哪里。这是日记中唯一一个波德卢布内没有保持冷静的场景。连笔迹学家都曾注意到的镇定，这时也离他而去，因为他失去了对自己生活和身体的控制。波德卢布内最终在莫斯科的一所监狱里找到了他的母亲。探视期间，她含泪告诉他，一个内务部法庭判处她八年监禁，“罪名是隐瞒社会出身”。他的反应既绝望又愤慨：“多可怕，八年。说起来这么容易，过起来却这么难。为了什么？！……人们还说这世上有正义。”日记条目以反抗的基调结束。它回响着苏联文学中熟悉的革命自由战士的语言，但波德卢布内将其转而针对苏联国家：“不，会有正义的。许多人以正义的名义牺牲了，只要社会存在，人们就会为正义而斗争。正义会到来的。真相会到来的。”

In his reaction to the arrest Stepan Podlubny’s extraordinary attachment to his mother became evident. He spent the next days and weeks trying to find her. Long lines formed every morning at the information office of the Moscow militia. To make it to the information window before it closed at 4 p.m. he had to be there shortly after five in the morning. Standing in a line extending for half a kilometer, watching the hundreds of other Muscovites who were searching for arrested relatives and loved ones, he discovered a world of people who were oblivious to the imperatives and the clichés of the official world: they were “absorbed in their own private concerns, for them the world outside does not exist.” Then it was his turn at the small square window: “An inexplicable terror came over me. My knees shook and buckled under me, my fingers trembled nervously. My heart raced . . . It was only after I got home that I fully realized the meaning of what had happened. A huge lump in my throat cut off my breath. I lost control of my muscles.” The official at the window had been unable to tell where his mother was. It was a unique scene in the diary in that Podlubny did not keep his cool. The presence of mind to which even the graphologist had attested eluded him, as he lost control over his life and his own body. Podlubny ultimately managed to locate his mother in a Moscow prison. During his visit she told him tearfully that an NKVD tribunal had sentenced her to eight years in prison “for concealment of social origins.” His reaction was desperate and indignant at once: “How horrible, eight years. It’s so easy to pronounce, but so hard to live through. And for what?! . . . And they say there is justice in this world.” The entry ended on a defiant note. It echoed the language of revolutionary freedom fighters familiar from Soviet literature, but Podlubny turned it against the Soviet state: “No, there will be justice. Many people have perished in the name of justice, and as long as society exists, people will be struggling for justice. Justice will come. The truth will come.”

母亲被捕后，波德卢布内的日记政治色彩变得更浓，他用尖锐的措辞谴责斯大林政权的政策。用他的话来说，为归来的极地探险队举行的宏大招待会是一场“前所未有的喧嚣”，目的仅仅是为了转移民众对党的首席理论家尼古拉·布哈林的审判和处决的注意力。在读了亨利克·显克微支描写公元一世纪罗马帝国的《君往何处去？》后，波德卢布内将斯大林描述为“我们的俄罗斯尼禄”，并专门针对他的个人崇拜写道：“看来，无端的赞美、将善行归功于某个人以及对他的神化，在我们的时代也是可能的，只是形式更为微妙。”

波德卢布内将他这一时期的日记条目称为对“对事实的自然主义记录”。从社会主义现实主义的历史信心来看，自然主义视角定义上就是悲观和堕落的。波德卢布内为他使用自然主义辩护。他写道，他的目的是以不同的角度呈现现实，从而使人们对惯常用来描述生活的辞藻产生陌生感。去外省小镇雅罗斯拉夫尔探望父亲的经历让他大开眼界。尽管他的父亲现在过着城市生活，但他不仅与其他工人共住一室，还和一头小猪以及成群的虫子和虱子同住。在雅罗斯拉夫尔郊区游览时，波德卢布内震惊地发现，这种生活条件似乎是常态。然而，所有他询问的人都回答说他们过得很好。波德卢布内写道，只有他作为到访局外人的“新鲜视角”，才能让他理解这些生活条件的“非人”本质。“我们不能这样生活，”他宣称。

显而易见，斯捷潘不再将他父亲肮脏的生活条件归咎于其落后的观念和意志薄弱。相反，这一条目和其他条目都流露出一种感觉：政权未能照顾那些真诚地为它效力的人。斯捷潘访问期间拍摄的一张父子合影表明两人已经达成和解，同时也展示了菲利普的新面貌。他西装革履，看起来像一个现代城市公民，其形象塑造得就像站在他身边的儿子一样。这张照片和波德卢布内在访问期间对他父亲的描述，与他早期将菲利普表现为一个可怜生物的描述形成了鲜明的对比。

After his mother’s arrest, Podlubny’s diary turned more political in character, as he denounced the policies of the Stalinist regime in acerbic terms. The grandiose reception of a returning team of polar explorers was, in his words, an “unprecedented hullabaloo” that served only the purpose of deflecting popular attention from the trial and execution of the party’s chief theoretician, Nikolai Bukharin. After reading Quo Vadis? by Henryk Sienkiewicz, which was situated in Imperial Rome in the first century a.d., Podlubny characterized Stalin as “our Russian Nero,” specifically addressing his personal cult: “It appears that the unjustified lavishing of praise and attribution of good deeds, as well as deification, are possible in our times too, if only in a more subtle form.”

Podlubny referred to his diary entries of this period as a “naturalist fixation of facts.” Seen through the lens of socialist realism’s historical confidence, the naturalist perspective was by definition pessimistic and degenerative. Podlubny defended his use of naturalism. His purpose, he wrote, was to cast reality in a different light and thus estrange people from the rhetoric they reflexively invoked to describe their lives. A visit to his father in the provincial town of Yaroslavl was eye-opening. Although his father now lived an urban life, he shared a room not only with other workers but also with a piglet and swarms of bugs and lice. On a tour through the outskirts of Yaroslavl Podlubny discovered with shock that such living conditions appeared to be the rule. Yet all the people he questioned replied that they were doing well. Only his “fresh perspective” as a visiting outsider, Podlubny wrote, allowed him to understand the “inhuman” nature of these living conditions. “We mustn’t live like this,” he declared.

Tellingly, Stepan no longer blamed his father’s backward outlook and weak will for his squalid living conditions. Instead, this and other entries resonated with a sense that the regime had failed to provide for people who had sincerely worked for its interests. A photograph of father and son, taken during Stepan’s visit, suggests that the two had made peace, and also presents a new view of Filip. Dressed in a suit and tie, he appears as a modern urban citizen, cast in the image of his son, who poses next to him. Both the photo and Podlubny’s descriptions of his father during the visit strikingly depart from his earlier representations of Filip as a wretched creature.

然而，以自然主义风格面对苏联现实是有代价的。这不仅是这些文字对波德卢布内安全的威胁问题；它们还破坏了他的自我形象，而他的自我形象在很大程度上建立在社会主义现实主义的人格概念之上。在1930年代后期的日记中，波德卢布内不得不面对一个事实：他在内心深处已经变成了一个“悲观主义者”，饱受意志力缺乏的折磨，而且他将自己转变为社会主义人格的尝试已经失败。在被迫放弃大学学业后，他思考着自己漫无目的、“无用”的生存状态：“没有目标的生活就像动物的生活！那是种什么样的生活？没有任何东西、任何人和任何事能给我道德支持。”这种“没有进步感”的生活加深了他的悲观情绪。他没有争取复学并重获开朗视角的事实，证明了他的意志病态：“我的意志力已经完全破碎，我的坚韧和忍耐，我的执着，甚至我的固执，都消失了。我失去了对自己的控制。”最后，还有他的个人生活问题。既然他即将满25岁，是时候结婚了，然而仅有的几个似乎可以交往的女孩都来自缺乏文化的阶级。

Yet to engage with Soviet reality in a naturalist style came at a price. It was not just a question of the danger that these writings posed for  Podlubny’s safety; they also undermined his self-image, which rested in large measure on socialist realist conceptions of the person. In his diary of the late 1930s Podlubny had to contend with the fact that he had become a “pessimist” at heart, plagued by a lack of willpower, and that his attempt to turn himself into a socialist personality had failed. Having been forced to give up his university studies, he pondered his aimless, “useless” existence: “Life without a goal is like an animal’s life! What sort of life is that? There is nothing, nothing and nobody to give me moral support.” This life, “without the feeling of progress,” deepened his pessimism. The fact that he did not fight to resume his studies and regain a cheerful perspective was evidence of a diseased will: “My willpower has been completely shattered, gone are my toughness and endurance, my persistence, indeed, my stubbornness. I have lost control over myself.” Finally, there was the issue of his personal life. Now that he was about to turn 25, it was time to get married, yet the few girls who seemed available were all from the less-cultured classes.

从这个卑微的地位，他嫉妒地观察着他曾经置身其中的大学生“圈子”。1938年春天，他的一个朋友弗拉基米尔·沃龙佐夫——两年前因其父亲被揭露为托洛茨基分子而被开除出共青团——被重新接纳进青年组织。他计划研究哲学并加入共产党。斯捷潘批评弗拉基米尔决定成为一名党务工作者；弗拉基米尔则责备斯捷潘的“利己主义”，认为他只向生活索取而不给予。对现有现实表达纯粹负面的观点招致了利己主义的指控，使波德卢布内与尼古拉·阿尼辛这类人处于同样的位置。阿尼辛是他在《真理报》印刷厂的学徒同伴，斯捷潘曾以同样的罪名向格别乌告发过他。从某种意义上说，波德卢布内政治日记中那种直言不讳本身就在不断破坏集体主义、乐观主义且始终奋斗的人格理想，而在他思考自己生活的失败时，他继续以这一理想来衡量自己。

From this lowly position he enviously observed the “milieu” of the university students in whose company he had once been. In the spring of 1938 a friend, Vladimir Vorontsov, who had been expelled from the Komsomol two years earlier because his father had been uncovered as a Trotskyist, was readmitted into the youth organization. He had plans to study philosophy and join the Communist party. Stepan criticized Vladimir for his decision to become a party apparatchik; Vladimir in turn chided Stepan for his “egoism,” for only taking from life but not giving. To voice purely negative views on existing reality invited charges of egoism, putting Podlubny in company with the likes of Nikolai Anisin, his fellow apprentice at the Pravda printing plant, whom he had denounced to the GPU on the same charge. In some sense the very outspokenness of Podlubny’s political diary thus kept undermining the ideal of the collectivist, optimistic, and always-striving personality against which he continued to measure himself when he contemplated the failure of his life.

母亲不在身边后，独自生活的波德卢布内继续使用他信赖的办法，以避免招惹苏联当局。特别是在国家节日前夜，他一定会住在外面。但他最终还是被捕了。波德卢布内的日记在1939年10月突然停止，就在德国和苏联入侵波兰后不久，他在日记中密切关注着这一事件。几天后，他打算协助他的堂表兄弟科尔内·克里沃鲁卡卖掉科尔内工作的钟表厂的零配件。波德卢布内认识一位钟表匠并让他对这笔交易产生了兴趣。然而，当三人见面完成交易时，钟表匠带来了警察。科尔内被控投机倒把，被判处五年劳改。斯捷潘因未向当局举报这位堂表兄弟而被判处十八个月劳改。他被带到莫斯科以东约六百英里的一个营地。1940年4月，他与其他身体健康的男子一起被转移到远北地区的佩乔拉。在那里，他们要修筑一条通往北极城市沃尔库塔的铁路。许多囚犯在极度繁重的劳动、严寒和营养不良的条件下丧生。波德卢布内之所以幸存下来，是因为他设法在营地管理部门为自己谋得了一席之地。他于1941年4月从营地获释，就在铁路建设完工前不久。

On his own without his mother, Podlubny continued to follow his trusted techniques for avoiding brushes with Soviet authorities. Especially on the nights before state holidays, he made sure to sleep away from home. But he was arrested in the end. Podlubny’s diary stops abruptly in October 1939, shortly after the German and Soviet invasion of Poland, which he followed attentively in his journal. A few days later he was to assist his cousin Kornei Krivoruka in selling off spare parts from the watch factory in which Kornei worked. Podlubny knew a watchmaker and got him interested in the deal. Yet when the three met to complete the transaction, the watchmaker brought the police along. Kornei was charged with speculation and sentenced to five years in a labor camp. Stepan was sentenced to eighteen months in a labor camp for failing to denounce his cousin to the authorities. He was taken to a camp about six hundred miles east of Moscow. In April 1940 he was transferred with other physically fit men to Pechora in the far north. There they were to build a railway track to the Arctic city of Vorkuta. Many prisoners perished under the conditions of extreme work, severe cold, and malnutrition. Podlubny survived because he managed to secure a place for himself in the camp administration. He was freed from the camp in April 1941, shortly before the railway construction was completed.
1941年6月初，就在德国入侵苏联前几天，波德卢布内应征入伍。由于他的犯罪记录，他未被允许在前方服役。从1941年10月起，他担任医务护理员，陪同预备役部队从西伯利亚前往前线。1944年，他被提升为医务中尉。波德卢布内之所以能晋升为军官，仅仅是因为他声称自己完成了医学学业并获得了文凭。
战争结束后，他在莫斯科定居。在那里他遇到了他未来的妻子卓娅，并于1947年结婚。波德卢布内的母亲于1940年提前从劳改营获释。战争结束后，她和菲利普搬进了儿子的公寓。菲利普·波德卢布内于1964年去世，叶夫罗西尼娅·丹尼洛夫娜于1974年去世。直到退休前，斯捷潘·波德卢布内一直在不同的苏联部委工作，大部分时间在卫生部担任行政人员。

In early June 1941, only days before Germany invaded the Soviet Union, Podlubny was called to military service. Because of his criminal record, he was not allowed to serve at the front. From October 1941 he worked as a medical orderly, accompanying reserve units from Siberia to the front. In 1944 he was promoted to the rank of lieutenant of medical service. Podlubny’s promotion to officer rank was possible only because he claimed to have completed his medical studies and received a diploma.

After the end of the war, he settled in Moscow. There he met his future wife, Zoya, and they married in 1947. Podlubny’s mother had obtained an early release from labor camp in 1940. Following the war she and Filip moved into their son’s apartment. Filip Podlubny died in 1964, Yefrosinia Danilovna in 1974. Until his retirement, Stepan Podlubny worked in different Soviet ministries, most of the time as an administrator in the ministry of health.
从劳改营获释后，波德卢布内（Podlubny）恢复了日记写作；他一直坚持写到1998年去世，享年84岁。然而，他关于战争和战后时期的日记缺乏那种刻画其20世纪30年代日记的戏剧性。值得注意的是，这些日记不再提及出身与行为之间的冲突。波德卢布内在苏联秩序中的地位问题似乎在战争期间和战后得到了解决，政权承认他为军官，并允许他在国家行政机构工作。
阅读波德卢布内战后的日记，只会更加突显他30年代日记项目的紧迫性——那种对灵魂状态的迫切关注、不断探寻的内省以及对自我的雕琢。

When released from the labor camp, Podlubny resumed writing his diary; he continued to do so until his death in 1998, at the age of 84. Yet his diaries from the war and the postwar period lack the drama characterizing his journal from the 1930s. Notably, they no longer mention the conflict between origins and deeds. It appears that the question of Podlubny’s standing in the Soviet order was resolved during and after the war, with the regime recognizing him as an army officer and allowing him to work in the state administration.

Reading Podlubny’s postwar diaries only underscores the urgency of his diary project of the 1930s—the pressing concern for the state of his soul, the searching in-trospection, and the work on his self.

我有幸与波德卢布内以及其他几位幸存的30年代日记作者交谈。20世纪90年代初我在莫斯科与他的最初几次接触是复杂且充满误解的。令我震惊的是，他竟然如此否定他在年轻时的日记中充分记录的对自我改造的追求。在我们的谈话中，他试图传达这样一种观点：他的日记是一个斯大林主义受害者的记录，其目的是为了记录他及其家人在那个残暴政权下的痛苦遭遇。这种信念促使他将日记存入历史档案馆，他称这一步是他为确立关于斯大林主义的真相所做出的个人贡献。
对于我根据他在档案馆的日记所提出的问题，波德卢布内反应很不耐烦。他觉得讨论他与父亲紧张的关系，或者他在日记中表达的关于落后、文化和理想人格形式的看法是毫无意义的。正如他所坚持的，他写的那些关于父亲的批评文字仅表达了“某些情绪”，但事实上他从未停止过对父亲的崇敬。

I had the good fortune to talk with Podlubny as well as several other surviving diarists from the 1930s. My initial encounters with him, in Moscow in the early 1990s, were complicated and fraught with misunderstandings. I was struck by the degree to which he disavowed the striving for self-transformation so amply documented in the diary of his youth. In our conversations he sought to convey the point that his diary was the document of a victim of Stalinism, and that its purpose had been to chronicle his and his family’s suffering at the hands of an inhuman regime. This conviction had prompted him to deposit the diary in a historical archive, a step he described as his personal contribution to establishing the truth about Stalinism.

Podlubny reacted impatiently to questions I had derived from reading his diary in the archive. He found it pointless to discuss his tense relationship with his father or the views he expressed in the diary about backwardness, culture, and ideal forms of selfhood. As he insisted, his critical writings about his father expressed only “certain moods,” but in fact he had never stopped venerating him.
作为重写其经历努力的一部分，波德卢布内在20世纪80年代花了几年时间制作了一个他30年代日记的修订版，对原稿中描述的事件、人物和思想增加了“必要的”注释。他修改了语言以赋予其更多的文学性，并删掉了他认为无用的段落。波德卢布内如此深信他修订版日记在“科学”和“艺术”上的优越性，以至于他甚至考虑过销毁原稿。

As part of his effort to rewrite his experience, Podlubny spent several years during the 1980s producing an edited version of his diaries of the 1930s, adding “necessary” commentary on events, people, and thoughts described in the original text. He edited the language to give it a more literary quality, and he dropped passages that he deemed useless. Podlubny was so convinced of the “scientific” and “artistic” superiority of the edited version of his diary that he even considered destroying the original.

鉴于齐娜伊达·德尼谢夫斯卡娅（Zinaida Denisevskaya）的日记及其命运，波德卢布内对待日记的态度是引人注目的。两位作者都生活在一个对其社会出身怀有敌意的政权之下；两人都经受过焦虑和怀疑，同时也表达过克服内心冲突的希望。1977年，德尼谢夫斯卡娅的日记被提交给国家档案馆，以此在苏联的记忆库中增加一名社会主义公民的声音。十多年后，波德卢布内改写了他的记录，以申明自己是苏联体制终身受害者的身份。这两个截然相反的日记行为之间跨越的时间，衡量了在此期间苏联政治体系所经历的合法性流失。波德卢布内通过改写自己年轻时代的经历，与无数其他斯大林时期的幸存者采取了相似的做法，这些幸存者开始从自身受害的角度来看待过去。诸如莫斯科新成立的“人民档案馆”等机构也鼓励他们这样做，该机构在呼吁民众提交其经历的回忆录时，也构建了这种经历所应呈现的形式。波德卢布内正是将日记存放在这个档案馆里。

Podlubny’s attitude toward his diary is remarkable in light of Zinaida Denisevskaya’s diary and its fate. Both authors had lived under a regime that looked upon their social origins with hostility; both suffered anxieties and doubts while also expressing hopes of overcoming their inner conflicts. In 1977 Denisevskaya’s diary was submitted to a state archive to add the voice of a socialist citizen to the Soviet memory house. A little more than a decade later Podlubny adapted his record to claim the status of a lifelong victim of the Soviet state. The span of time between these two opposite diaristic gestures measures the loss of legitimacy that the Soviet political system underwent in the interim. In writing himself out of the time of his youth, Podlubny acted in concert with countless other survivors of the Stalin period who came to view their past in self-victimizing terms. They were encouraged by institutions such as the newly established “People’s archive” in Moscow, which in appealing to the population to submit memoirs of their experience also structured the shape this experience was to take. It was in this archive that Podlubny deposited his diary.

同上（1935年9月18日）。波德卢布内之所以能被医学院录取，很大程度上归功于他虚构的工人出身。在一次数学预考失败后，他去找院长请求重考。由于他声称自己是无产阶级，这一请求得到了批准。在第二次考试中，老师给了波德卢布内一份书面作业，然后没看结果就给了他及格的分数（波德卢布内访谈录，1992年6月23日）。直到1935年，苏联高等教育的录取都受到社会配额的管制，这些配额严重向无产阶级背景的候选人倾斜。其目的是促进工人阶级知识分子的产生。1928年，四分之一的苏联学生具有无产阶级背景；到1935年，这一比例已上升至45%。见奥斯卡·安韦勒（Oskar Anweiler）和卡尔-海因茨·鲁夫曼（Karl-Heinz Ruffmann）编，《苏俄文化政策》（Kulturpolitik der Sowjetunion）（斯图加特：克朗纳出版社，1973年），第62–63页。 1935年12月，政府法令宣布，所有苏联公民，不论出身，都有权在高等教育机构学习。然而，这一新政策并没有结束对阶级异己分子的歧视。见菲茨帕特里克著，《归属阶级》（Ascribing Class），第757–758页。
en:
Ibid. (9/18/1935). Podlubnyi owed his admission to the Medical Insti-
tute largely to his fictitious worker origins. Upon failing a preparatory
math exam he went to the dean and asked to be reexamined. The re-
quest was granted because of his claim to be a proletarian. At his sec-
ond exam, the teacher handed Podlubnyi a written assignment and
then, without looking at the results, gave him a satisfactory grade (in-
terview with Podlubnyi, 6/23/1992). Until 1935 admission to Soviet
higher education was regulated by social quotas that heavily favored
candidates of proletarian background. The purpose was to facilitate
the creation of a working-class intelligentsia. In 1928 one-quarter of
all Soviet students were of proletarian background; by 1935 their share
had risen to 45 percent. Kulturpolitik der Sowjetunion, ed. Oskar
Anweiler and Karl-Heinz Ruffmann (Stuttgart: Kröner, 1973), 62–63.
In December 1935 a government decree proclaimed the right of all So-
viet citizens, regardless of origins, to study at institutes of higher edu-
cation. This new policy, however, did not put an end to discrimina-
tion against class aliens. Fitzpatrick, “Ascribing Class,” 757–758.

波德卢布内的行为符合戈尔福·亚历克索普洛斯所说的“仪式性哀求”，这是许多阶级异己分子的做法，他们在给苏联政权的请愿书中强调自己的无助，以博取当局的照顾。见亚历克索普洛斯著，《斯大林的弃民》（Stalin’s Outcasts）。然而他的案例也表明，这种自我呈现超出了与政权的官方互动，影响了波德卢布内的自我意识。

the authorities’ care. Alexopoulos, Stalin’s Outcasts. Yet his case also
shows this self-representation extending beyond official interaction
with the regime, impinging on Podlubnyi’s sense of self.
